title: Fleas on Dogs: How to Check, Treat Your Dog and Clear Your House
seoTitle: Fleas on Dogs: How to Check, Treat and Prevent
description: Fleas on dogs: what they look like, the wet paper towel test, a 3-step treatment plan for your dog and house, and why home remedies fall short.
secondaryKeywords: what do fleas on dogs look like

faq.q: How do I know if my dog has fleas?
faq.a: Part the hair over the hips, the base of the tail and the thighs and look for tiny moving insects or black specks. Comb the specks onto a damp white paper towel: flea dirt dissolves into a reddish brown smear.
Fleas bite people, but they infest pets, not humans; their life cycle runs on dogs and cats and in the home. People can carry fleas indoors on clothing, which is how indoor-only pets get them.

faq.q: How do I get rid of fleas in my house?
faq.a: Treat every pet with a vet-recommended product, wash bedding in hot water and vacuum carpets, furniture and cracks often. Heavy infestations may need a household spray with an insect growth regulator, and pets should stay on flea control for 3 to 6 months.

faq.q: Do home remedies for fleas on dogs work?
faq.a: They don't break the flea life cycle. About 95% of a flea population lives in the home as eggs, larvae and pupae, so a vet-recommended product for every pet plus house cleaning is what works.

faq.q: Why does my dog still have fleas after treatment?
faq.a: Usually because pupae in the home keep hatching for weeks, another pet wasn't treated, or the product wasn't applied correctly. VCA says there is no evidence that fleas have become resistant to insecticides.
